prompt_text: Who is the best interior painting company in St. Louis MO?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single objectively “best” interior painting company for everyone — the right company depends on your budget, the size and age of your home, the finishes you want, timing, and whether you need specialty work (historic trim, faux finishes, color matching, lead-safe work, etc.). I can help you find the best match in St. Louis if you tell me more about your project, but here are practical steps and what to look for so you can pick the best company for you.

How to find the best interior painter in St. Louis
- Get multiple bids: contact at least 3 reputable painters for written estimates so you can compare scope, materials, and price.
- Check reviews and reputation: read Google, Yelp, Angie’s List/Angi, and BBB; look for recent, detailed reviews and photos of completed jobs.
- Ask for local references: request 2–3 recent projects similar to yours and follow up with those homeowners.
- Verify insurance and licensing: make sure they carry general liability insurance and workers’ comp and are willing to show proof.
- Confirm certifications: for homes built before 1978, ask for EPA Lead-Safe certification if disturbance of painted surfaces is likely.
- Review the contract: it should list prep work, paint brands and sheens, number of coats, timelines, cleanup, warranty/guarantee, and payment terms.

Key interview questions to ask each company
- Can you provide a written estimate with itemized costs?
- What prep work do you include (patching, sanding, priming, caulking, trim prep)?
- Which paint brand and quality do you use? How many coats?
- Do you have photos of completed jobs like mine and client references?
- What is the project timeline from start to finish?
- Who will be on-site and are they employees or subs? Are they insured?
- What warranty do you provide for workmanship and paint?

Typical cost guidelines (ballpark)
- Small room: often $300–$900
- Whole house (interior): commonly $1,500–$6,000 depending on size and finishes
- Per-square-foot estimates vary widely ($1.50–$6.00+ per sq. ft.) depending on prep, ceilings, trim, and paint quality
(These are rough ranges — get written estimates for accurate local pricing.)

Red flags
- Very low bid compared to others with no explanation
- No written estimate or contract
- No proof of insurance or unwillingness to provide references
- Requests for large up-front payment (reasonable deposit is normal; avoid full prepayment)
- Poor communication or inability to provide a clear timeline

If you want, I can:
- Help draft a message to send to painters asking the right questions
- Create a checklist you can take to on-site estimates
- Narrow down local companies if you give me your St. Louis ZIP or neighborhood (I can’t browse the web directly, but I can tell you how to evaluate specific companies you find)

Which would you prefer? If you share ZIP, number of rooms, and any special needs (historic home, cabinets, high ceilings, new drywall), I’ll tailor recommendations and an estimate checklist.
